generation.raw_text: {"status":"answered","answer":"Mendel's monohybrid experiment involved crossing two pure-breeding pea plants that differed in a single trait. For example, he crossed a pure-breeding yellow seed plant (YY) with a pure-breeding green seed plant (yy). In the first generation (F1), all offspring had yellow seeds, indicating that yellow is the dominant trait. When these F1 plants were self-pollinated, the second generation (F2) showed a 3:1 ratio of yellow to green seeds. This experiment demonstrates Mendel's Law of Dominance, which states that in a pair of alleles, one is dominant and masks the expression of the other, recessive allele.","selected_evidence_ids":["E2","E3","E4","E5"],"citations":[{"evidence_id":"E2","pdf_page":191,"textbook_page":182},{"evidence_id":"E3","pdf_page":192,"textbook_page":183},{"evidence_id":"E4","pdf_page":193,"textbook_page":184},{"evidence_id":"E5","pdf_page":195,"textbook_page":186}],"missing_information":[]}
